body: Zee Entertainment was a high-quality, cash-generative media franchise, but promoter Subhash Chandra's Essel group borrowed against Zee shares to fund infrastructure, power and other ventures. On 25 Jan 2019 Zee fell ~26-33% intraday on reports linking the group to an investigation and on lenders invoking pledges; Essel group listed stocks (Dish TV, Zee Media, Siti) fell 10-30%. Pledges rose to ~59% then ~90% of promoter holding; promoter debt ~Rs 7,000 cr (Oct 2019) after asset sales. Zee hit a ~6-year low in Sep-Oct 2019 (-60%+ from the ~Rs 600 Jan 2018 peak). Promoter stake fell from ~42% to ~4% as lenders and promoters sold. Later: a Zee FD/letter of comfort for group loans (Yes Bank) surfaced; Invesco fight (2021); the Sony merger collapsed (Jan 2024); SEBI orders on fund diversion (2023) and a separate Aug 2026 order barring Subhash Chandra and Punit Goenka for a year over an unauthorised Hyderabad land pledge (stock -13%). Visible flags: rising promoter pledge %, group holdco debt unrelated to Zee's business, MF FMPs lending against promoter shares, listed company comforts/guarantees for group debt, related-party advances. Lesson: a great business can be a bad stock if the promoter is levered elsewhere; pledges >25% and rising are a disqualifier.

data.early_signals: promoter pledge 59%->90%; group infra debt; MF loans against shares; letters of comfort
data.lesson: Pledge trend is a governance + forced-selling risk

title: Zee / Essel group pledge crisis (2019)
